title: Tor-independent scalar exchange for perfect derived coinduction
statement:
Let $P\to A$ and $P\to T$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings and put $A_T=A\otimes_PT$. Assume $A$ and $T$ are Tor independent over $P$, meaning $A[0]\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T\simeq A_T[0]$. Use ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], derived scalar extension [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor], and derived coinduction $C_A^P$ with its precomposition action [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. Write $U$ and $U_T$ for restriction along $P\to A$ and $T\to A_T$, and $\epsilon_M:UC_A^P(M)\to M$ for the evaluation-at-one counit [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction]. For every $N\in D(A)$ the canonical tensor comparison is an isomorphism
$$\theta_N:U_T(N\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}(UN)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T.$$
For every $M\in D(P)$ there is a canonical natural map in $D(A_T)$
$$\gamma_M:C_A^P(M)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_T\longrightarrow C_{A_T}^T(M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T),$$
characterized as the adjoint of $(\epsilon_M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T)\circ\theta_{C_A^P(M)}$. If $A[0]$ is perfect over $P$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], then $\gamma_M$ is an isomorphism for every unbounded $M$. For a bounded finite projective resolution $F^\bullet\to A[0]$ and a finite projective $P$-module $L$ in degree zero, its underlying $T$-map, under $\theta$, is the localization of
$$\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(F,L)\otimes_PT\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_T^\bullet(F\otimes_PT,L\otimes_PT),\qquad(h\otimes t)(z\otimes s)=ts(h(z)\otimes1).$$
Here $F\otimes_PT$ resolves $A_T$ by Tor independence. The comparison is natural in derived morphisms of $M$ and in maps between such resolutions. It is compatible with further scalar extension $T\to T'$ whenever $A$ and $T'$ are Tor independent over $P$; after the canonical tensor associators, direct and successive comparisons agree. No flatness of $P\to T$, surjectivity of $P\to A$, Noetherianity, or boundedness of $M$ is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an $A$-K-flat representative $Q$ of $N$ and a $P$-K-flat resolution $s:E\to UQ$. The cited resolution theorem supplies both choices. Computing $A[0]\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T$ on a free resolution of $A$, the definition of Tor in def-weil-pbc-tor-modules turns the hypothesis into $\operatorname{Tor}_i^P(A,T)=0$ for $i>0$. This and lem-pc-tor-independent-kflat-resolution-tensor make $s\otimes_PT$ a quasi-isomorphism. The normalized ordinary balancing isomorphism of lem-pc-base-tensor-ordinary-iso identifies $Q\otimes_PT$ with $U_T(Q\otimes_A A_T)$, by $q\otimes t\mapsto q\otimes(1\otimes t)$, after the degree-zero tensor flips. Hence the comparison $c_N:(UN)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T\to U_T(N\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_T)$ represented by $s\otimes_PT$ and this balancing is invertible. Set $\theta_N=c_N^{-1}$. The scalar-extension functor and its canonical resolution comparisons show that this is independent of $Q,E,s$ and natural on derived morphisms. This is the comparison of the source, with its direction inverted.

source.place: Tag 0661 (lemma-base-change-comparison), with equation-comparison-map immediately before it; construction on an A-K-flat complex and a base-K-flat resolution.

proof.text: Apply the coinduction adjunction for $T\to A_T$ to $X=C_A^P(M)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A_T$ and $Y=M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T$. The map $b_M=(\epsilon_M\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T)\circ\theta_{C_A^P(M)}:U_TX\to Y$ has a unique adjunct $\gamma_M:X\to C_{A_T}^T(Y)$. In particular $\epsilon_Y\circ U_T\gamma_M=b_M$. For $u:M\to M'$ the naturality equations of $\epsilon$ and $\theta$ give $b_{M'}\circ U_T(C_A^P(u)\otimes1)=(u\otimes1)\circ b_M$. Naturality of the adjunction bijection therefore gives naturality of $\gamma$ on arbitrary derived morphisms. Neither this construction nor step 1 used perfectness.

source.place: section-base-change-trivial-duality, equation-base-change and the paragraph defining it by the evaluation counit.

proof.text: Identify the underlying map by transposing twice, first through coinduction and then through the tensor-Hom adjunction of lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal. The inverse coinduction correspondence of lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-derived-hom-adjunction sends $g$ to $x\mapsto(a\mapsto g(ax))$. Thus the transpose of $U_T\gamma_M$, after $\theta$, is scalar extension of the evaluation $R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,M)\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}A\to M$: evaluation at $a$ is evaluation at $1$ after the precomposition action by $a$. This is an identity of the cited Hom-complex correspondences, hence remains true after localization, not only on degree-zero cohomology. After replacing $A\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T$ by $A_T[0]$, this is exactly the evaluation transpose defining the canonical derived-Hom scalar comparison. For a perfect-source representative its localization is the normalized $\chi$ of def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map: uncurrying its coordinate formula gives $h,z,t,s\mapsto ts(h(z)\otimes1)$, the same scalar-extended evaluation. Uniqueness of the two adjunction correspondences identifies these maps. This identifies an already constructed map in $D(A_T)$; it does not manufacture an algebra action from a map in $D(T)$.

source.place: lemma-check-base-change-is-iso, proof: apply restriction and identify equation-base-change with equation-base-change-RHom by the evaluation adjunctions; explicit uncurrying verification.

proof.text: Assume $A[0]$ perfect over $P$, and choose a bounded finite projective resolution $F\to A[0]$ and an arbitrary K-flat representative $Q$ of $M$. The cited resolution and bounded-projective extension results make $F$ K-flat and $F\otimes_PT$ bounded projective; Tor independence makes the latter a resolution of $A_T[0]$: its cohomology in degree $-i$ is $\operatorname{Tor}_i^P(A,T)$ by def-weil-pbc-tor-modules, zero for $i>0$, and $H^0$ is $A\otimes_PT$ by right exactness. The representative factorization in def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map computes the underlying map identified in step 3 by $\chi:\operatorname{Hom}_P^\bullet(F,Q)\otimes_PT\to\operatorname{Hom}_T^\bullet(F\otimes_PT,Q\otimes_PT)$. Lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-kflat makes its source compute the derived scalar extension, and lem-pc-perfect-ring-hom-scalar-extension says $\chi$ is a chain isomorphism. Thus $U_T\gamma_M$ is an isomorphism for arbitrary unbounded $M$. Conservativity in lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction proves $\gamma_M$ invertible in $D(A_T)$. In particular take $Q=L[0]$, K-flat by bounded projectivity. The defining coordinate equation for $\chi$, flipping the degree-zero $T$ factor, is precisely $(h\otimes t)(z\otimes s)=ts(h(z)\otimes1)$, the requested localized formula. No flatness of $P\to T$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 0A6A (lemma-base-change-RHom), equation-base-change-RHom and case (1); normalized finite-projective representative formula.

proof.text: For a chain map $a:F'\to F$ between augmented finite projective resolutions, the two comparison composites have the same value $ts(h(a(z))\otimes1)$ on $h\otimes t,z\otimes s$. For a target chain map $v:L\to L'$ both give $ts(v(h(z))\otimes1)$. These equalities on every Hom-coordinate and pure tensor prove the two naturality squares for $\chi$. Localizing these chain squares and using the canonical representative identifications in def-pc-perfect-rhom-base-change-map proves the asserted resolution compatibility; target derived naturality already holds for every $M$ by step 2. Thus no choice of resolution or of a lift of multiplication on $F$ changes the map.

source.place: equation-base-change-RHom, functoriality in both variables; explicit coordinate verification for the chosen resolutions.

proof.text: Let $T\to T'$ and put $A_{T'}=A\otimes_PT'$. Derived scalar associativity identifies $A_T\otimes_T^{\mathbf L}T'$ with $A\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T'$, by first identifying $A_T$ with $A\otimes_P^{\mathbf L}T$. Thus it is $A_{T'}[0]$, and the second square is Tor independent too. Use the scalar associators normalized by $((x\otimes t)\otimes t')\mapsto x\otimes tt'$. The two successive balancing comparisons of step 1 agree with the direct one: their ordinary balanced maps have this same formula, and the canonical derived comparisons preserve it. Transpose the successive $\gamma$ composite through the final coinduction adjunction. Twice substituting $\epsilon\circ U\gamma=(\epsilon\otimes1)\theta$ from step 2 cancels the intermediate counit against its defining adjunct. After these associators the result is $(\epsilon_M\otimes_PT')\theta^{P,T'}_{C_A^P(M)}$, the transpose of the direct $\gamma$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves equality. This also proves the identity case (the scalar unit is multiplication).
